gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-biorhyme: BioRhyme reads bookish and refined, its curves ending like brush strokes lifted early, capitals spaced wide. BioRhyme keeps a long page gentle, while Oldtimer's full-width strokes give the heading a flat, commanding look.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-biorhyme-expanded: Wide, stately, unhurried: BioRhyme Expanded breaks each word into separate letters, with an open e. Oldtimer commands with round, uniform forms; the classic serif body is built for reading.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-biz-udmincho: BIZ UDMincho is a traditional serif with shallow terminal curls. Its wide gaps keep a long page unhurried, a quiet foil to Oldtimer, whose strokes never taper where they meet or end.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-copse: Literary in feel, Copse lets daylight through every curved opening, while Oldtimer's round forms and flat, stencil-cut strokes stand firm above it. Sizing the classic serif body up a notch would suit it.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-cutive: Refined and literary, Cutive spreads its running text wide, with a generous opening in the c. And Oldtimer's single-weight outlines, round as open parentheses, sit above it with a classic, commanding confidence.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-david-libre: Oldtimer's round, parenthesis-like forms never swell or thin. David Libre follows with hanging open terminals, dignified and refined, so a long stretch of text moves along gently.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-enriqueta: Enriqueta reads literary and dignified, its chalk-like curves stopping well before they close. And Oldtimer's crossbars, as heavy as its stems, give the page a firm, commanding opening above that softer classic serif.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-fenix: Fenix is an editorial text serif whose curves end before turning inward. Oldtimer does best at commanding attention, its strokes uniform as drawn wire, while Fenix does best at carrying the words.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-gentium-plus: Oldtimer's round forms and uniform strokes, even on the diagonals, look like parentheses. Gentium Plus brings a refined classic serif with wide-mouthed c shapes, and that gentle openness is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-gowun-batang: Oldtimer's stroke ends are as wide as its middles, round and commanding. Gowun Batang, a classic serif with terminals cut back to leave a big gap, makes the pair feel refined and literary.
